key_insight: RFC Bench is a paragraph-level, reference-free benchmark that captures dispersed contextual cues in real financial news and adds paired original/perturbed examples to diagnose model sensitivity to subtle misinformation.
problem_solved: Detecting financial misinformation without relying on external references is hard because meaning in news often emerges from dispersed, subtle cues across a paragraph; existing evaluations do not test this realistic, context-dependent challenge or provide diagnostic paired inputs.
method: Construct RFC Bench operating at the paragraph level to preserve dispersed contextual signals in financial news.
Define two complementary tasks: (1) reference-free misinformation detection (single-paragraph labels) and (2) comparison-based diagnosis using paired original vs. perturbed paragraphs.
Evaluate large language models on both tasks to reveal performance patterns and model weaknesses in realistic, context-dependent settings.
impact: RFC Bench gives AI/ML practitioners a realistic, fine-grained tool to evaluate and improve models' robustness to subtle, contextual financial misinformation, enabling better model selection, tuning, and targeted defenses.
visual_elements: Dataset flowchart: news collection → paragraph extraction → perturbation → paired examples
Annotated paragraph diagram: highlighted dispersed cues (phrases, numbers, hedges) that determine truthfulness
Comparison panel: side-by-side original vs. perturbed paragraph with model verdicts to show diagnostic task
Bar/heatmap chart: model performance across the two tasks to visualize strengths and weaknesses
paper_title: All That Glisters Is Not Gold: A Benchmark for Reference-Free Counterfactual Financial Misinformation Detection
paper_authors: Yuechen Jiang, Zhiwei Liu, Yupeng Cao, Yueru He, Ziyang Xu
